title: Backing Bill Robinson and other acts
summary: Lunceford's band spent 22 weeks of theaters backing Bojangles Robinson, and also backed chorus lines and acts like Buck and Bubbles.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: One of the stars we backed was Bill Robinson, Bojangles. We did about 20 -- about 22 weeks of theaters with Bill Robinson, and our main thing was to back him, and he -- he had a pianist who traveled with him, Putney Dandridge and, of course, we -- there were certain recordings that we did that he liked, and he liked to tap dance to these things. One of them was Ain't She Sweet. And we used to sing that and play it softly, very softly, and he would come out and tap dance to it, and he liked -- For Pancers Only. We used to do that for him.

But we played it very soft, because he was a great artist, I thought, you know. I always used to watch this man perform, and he really had something going there. He could really reach the people. We played lots of theaters with him all through the Middle West, through Texas. There was a chain of theaters through Texas -- I think Majestic Theaters, I think, was the name; I'm not sure of that chain -- and we played quite a few theaters throughout the country. We did 22 straight weeks of theaters with him, Lunceford's band and --
What other stars did you work with with Lunceford?

Well, he would -- he would have been the most prominent star that we worked for, but we used to -- we used to always back choruses, girls, chorus girls, and this would be at the Apollo Theater and theaters of this sort. And now, we would play the music for quite a few of their acts, like Buck & Bubbles and acts of this sort back there then, John Bubbles and Buck Washington, his partner.

So we played for quite a few acts, and they were fine back there acts, then in -- I can't even recall the name of all the acts, but some of them were outstanding in my mind, for instance, as the two I named, you know.
